votes.evidence:
Premise traced and confirmed in the worktree.

Frontend (products/review_hog/frontend/CodeReviewScene.tsx:1048-1071): the Stamphog row renders a fixed title/description and a LemonSwitch. The only conditional is `disabledReason` at :1063-1069, which fires solely when `settings && !settings.stamphog_connected && !settings.stamphog_review_inbox_prs`. `stamphog_connected` is read nowhere else in the file (grep: :1066 is the sole use), so in the on+disconnected state the row is byte-identical to a healthy one. The in-code comment at :1064-1065 shows this state is reachable by design (opt-out must not dead-end).

Serializer contract (products/review_hog/backend/api/settings.py:50-53) says: "When false ... the UI renders it disabled with a pointer to connect the Stamphog GitHub App." The UI honors this only when the toggle is off; when on, there is neither disabled state nor pointer.

Backend consequence: receivers.py:126-138 queues `_start_stamphog_review` whenever `settings.stamphog_review_inbox_prs` is true, with no connection check. The Celery task `process_inbox_pr_review` (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1137-1152) resolves the config with `repository__iexact=repository, enabled=True, connected_by_user_id__isnull=False` + `.exclude(installation_id="")`, and on `None` returns after one info log `stamphog_inbox_pr_repo_not_reviewable` (:1150-1152). No run row, no PR comment, nothing user-visible.

Reachability of on+disconnected: after a user opts in while connected, repo configs flip to `enabled=False` on GitHub App uninstall (tasks.py:780-790), on repo removal from the installation (tasks.py:705-716), and on soft-delete via the API (presentation/views.py:225-234). Each makes `has_reviewable_repo_config` (products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:120-125) return False while the toggle stays on.

Per-repo gap: `has_reviewable_repo_config` is team-wide (`.exists()` over any synced+enabled repo, facade/api.py:120-125), whereas the task gate is per-repository (tasks.py:1140-1146). A team connected for repo A with an inbox PR against repo B reads `stamphog_connected=true`, shows a healthy row, and no-ops silently. This case needs no connection lapse at all.
votes.refutation: Attempted refutations: (1) Looked for a second read of `stamphog_connected` or any warning/hint element in CodeReviewScene.tsx or the review_hog frontend logic - none exists; :1066 is the only use. (2) Looked for a user-visible artifact on the backend no-op path (status comment, run row, notification) - the task returns at tasks.py:1152 after an info log only. (3) Checked whether on+disconnected is unreachable - it is reachable through three disconnect paths (uninstall, repo removal, soft-delete) after opt-in, and the per-repo mismatch is reachable for any multi-repo team with no lapse. (4) Checked whether the Stamphog scene covers this - it is a separate scene; the review_hog settings surface gives no signal. One caveat against the suggested fix, not the finding: `get_stamphog_connected` fails soft to False on a stamphog-DB read error (settings.py:72-81), so a warning hint keyed on `!stamphog_connected` would also appear during a transient outage. Blast radius is narrow (missing feedback, no wrong action, no data loss), which is why this is should_fix rather than must_fix.

votes.evidence:
Worktree /Users/woutut/.worktrees/posthog/frozen-75215.

UI state confirmed: products/review_hog/frontend/CodeReviewScene.tsx:1059-1069 — the Stamphog row's only conditional is `disabledReason`, gated on `settings && !settings.stamphog_connected && !settings.stamphog_review_inbox_prs`. When the toggle is ON and `stamphog_connected` is false the condition is false, so the row renders exactly as a healthy setup (no hint, no tint); `stamphog_connected` is read nowhere else in the scene (grep, single hit at line 1066).

Trigger reachability in production (angle 3):
1. On-then-disconnected is reachable. `has_reviewable_repo_config` (products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:113-125) filters `enabled=True`, and the Stamphog repo-config viewset's DELETE is a soft-disable that sets `enabled=False` (products/stamphog/backend/presentation/views.py:225-233); PATCH `enabled=false` does the same (views.py:236-239, serializer field `enabled` at serializers.py:78). So a user who turned the toggle on while connected, then removed/disabled their only repo, lands in toggle=true / stamphog_connected=false. The settings serializer (products/review_hog/backend/api/settings.py:21-81) has no `validate` cross-checking `stamphog_review_inbox_prs` against `stamphog_connected`, so a PATCH can also set it true directly while disconnected.
2. Per-repo gap is reachable. The inbox PR's repository comes from the task (`task.repository`, products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:106) and the PR URL; the queued task gates on a config for that exact repo (`repository__iexact=repository, enabled=True, connected_by_user_id__isnull=False`, products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1136-1146) and returns silently on miss (`stamphog_inbox_pr_repo_not_reviewable`, tasks.py:1150-1152), while `stamphog_connected` is team-wide (facade/api.py:120-125). A project with Stamphog on repo A and inbox tasks targeting repo B shows the toggle as healthy and never reviews.

Backend consequence: receivers.py:126-139 dispatches on the toggle alone; `_start_stamphog_review` (receivers.py:200-231) documents the repo gating as a "silent no-op" inside the Celery task. No PR comment, no run row, no UI surface reports it.
votes.refutation: Tried: (a) maybe the backend rejects enabling the toggle when disconnected — no, ReviewUserSettingsSerializer has no such validation and stamphog_connected is a read-only method field. (b) maybe repo configs can't be disabled after connect — no, DELETE soft-disables (views.py:225-233) and PATCH can flip `enabled`. (c) maybe stamphog_connected already matches the task gate — no, it is team-wide `.exists()` vs a per-repository `iexact` filter in the task. (d) maybe some other UI/error surface reports the no-op — the task only logs at info level and returns; nothing user-facing. Refutation fails on all fronts. Severity kept at should_fix rather than must_fix because it is a missing status signal, not data loss, and the user can work around it by checking Stamphog's own repository settings.
